items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...There was a lady, Miss Murphy. She was a toll keeper. And she, you had to pay her... But we used to go in on the trolley.

ctx.x: The boats were right there close to you. Yes. They were closer. Closer than they are now.

It was better. That was a poor man. The river was a poor man's west end. Because west end, they had to go out there in a trolley. And you had to pay toll to go out there. Yes. At Metairie. There was a lady, Miss Murphy. She was a toll keeper. And she, you had to pay her, I don't know whether it was two minutes, 15 cents, something like that, to go through. But we used to go in on the trolley. And the child would go out to West End. He used to lose his band. See, it was way out in the air, out in the water. Oh,…

The kids go in swimming down there? Well, I mean, you take on a Sunday afternoon. Yes. All the families go out on the riverfront. And there was one girl named Bebe Harrison. She used to jump, I mean, dive off the shed. Run and dive off the top of the shed.
